analysis:
The only changed file is .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py, a CI test harness for the threat-review tooling. The PR adds offline unit tests: a Bedrock 'workload' call policy with plan_calls admission, a 500-call emergency ceiling, 16384 output tokens, and a 600s read timeout with single-attempt SDK retries. It also adds invalid-config rejection tests, end-to-end Scanner tests with 31 and 62 source batches, and status_body tests that require explicit human review for incomplete final results. The clean() merge policy is asserted to return False for errors, limited files, pending depth, unmet coverage, and an incomplete integration. There are no changes to provider, coordinator, App Attest, key, or encryption code, so the canonical provider threat IDs (TB-002, TB-011, T-052..T-058) are not touched.

Security-relevant observations: the tests encode fail-closed behavior. Budget stops raise BudgetStopped without backup fallback. Invalid policy, ceiling, or token values raise ReviewUnavailable before any request is made. Usage is recorded without source content. Unplanned native calls are rejected. The tests use synthetic data and no secrets. The tests cannot show that the production modules (threat_review/bedrock.py, budget_scan.py, budget_runner.py) implement these behaviors, because that source was not supplied. The diff also does not show whether the CI workflow's environment enables the workload policy or whether the cost ceiling is appropriate. Both are unverified contracts for any pass that sees the non-test source files. No regression is identifiable in the supplied test-only change.
